webmcp/declarative/*.description: the declarative API of WebMCP (the `toolname`, `tooldescription`, `toolparamdescription` and `toolautosubmit` attributes of the forms, `SubmitEvent.agentInvoked` and `respondWith()`, the `:tool-form-active` and `:tool-submit-active` pseudo-classes), which only the explainer (https://github.com/webmachinelearning/webmcp/blob/main/declarative-api-explainer.md) and Chromium define: the specification defines the imperative API, which is implemented

service-workers/service-worker/unregiste.description: Runs until the maximum duration of the runner (1 minute): Clear-Site-Data is not implemented, so it cannot abort the evaluation of a service worker script that loops forever

html/webappapis/scripting/events/compile.description: Runs until the maximum duration of the runner (1 minute): a test needs window.open() and never completes, while another one reloads the iframe from its load event handler, so the event loop is never idle and the harness timeout (virtual clock) never fires

html/semantics/permission-element/*.description: the permission elements (`<permission>`, `<geolocation>`, `<install>`, `<usermedia>`, camera/microphone) proposed by the WICG Page Embedded Permission Control incubation: they are not part of the HTML Standard, and only Chromium implements them; most of the tests check their rendering (reftests, bounded CSS properties, icons) or need permission prompts

css/css-masking/clip-path/animations/cli.description: reftest whose screenshot is taken in the animation frame after the effect of the animation is replaced: depending on the timing of the frames, the first or the second step of the new effect is painted

speculation-rules/prerender/service-work.description: the first subtest creates the prerendered page right after `service_worker_unregister_and_register()`, which does not wait for the worker to be activated: a navigation is only controlled by an active worker (https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#on-fetch-request-algorithm), so nothing makes the prerendered page controlled. It is when the activation ends before the prerendering (it passes locally); on the loaded CI agents the page is not controlled and its fetch of `ping` gets 404 Not Found instead of `pong`

notifications/registration-association.h.description: `prepareActiveServiceWorker()` awaits `navigator.serviceWorker.ready`, which is resolved once per container (https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#navigator-service-worker-ready): in the first subtest it is already resolved with the registration of the setup, so it does not wait for the new registration to be activated. The second subtest calls `showNotification()` on the new registration, which rejects with a `TypeError` while its active worker is null (https://notifications.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-serviceworkerregistration-shownotification), so the result depends on whether the activation ended first (it failed 2 runs of 5 locally)

fetch/stale-while-revalidate/fetch-sw.ht.description: the test expects the message that the service worker posts for the second fetch to arrive before the response of a later fetch, which nothing orders: the worker posts it after an awaited `clients.matchAll()` in a `waitUntil()` that runs concurrently with `respondWith(fetch(...))`, and `clients.matchAll()` queues a task on the event loop of each window client to read its window data (https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#clients-matchall), while the stale response of the second fetch and the revalidation can complete first. When the first revalidation check already sees the 2 requests, the page checks the count before the message: `assert_equals(service_worker_count, 2)` fails with 1 (it passes locally, and failed on the loaded Linux arm64 CI runners)

page-lifecycle/worker-dispay-none.tentat.description: the dedicated workers of a frozen document are not paused (https://wicg.github.io/page-lifecycle/#worker-changes): freezing a document defers its own tasks and timers, but the event loops of its workers have no paused state, so the workers of the frozen iframe keep posting their messages. The test fails when more than one message of a worker arrives between the freeze and the resume, which depends on the timing, so it is not run
